title: MCP grant-grammar separator collision
severity: Medium (HIGH if attacker-influenced MCP server naming is in scope)

provenance.found_by: NorthWoods Sentinel Labs (NWS swarm, run by Margin, for Rob Chuvala)
provenance.source: GitHub the-metafactory/cortex, issue comment 5084213029 (NWS execution-boundary review, round 2, against cortex v6.13.0)

finding: grants use a server/server.tool grammar, and server names are parsed as the first __-delimited segment - but nothing forbids '.' or '__' inside a server name. A server named github.read_file matches a per-tool grant github.read_file via grants.includes(server); a server named github__evil (tool mcp__github__evil__x) parses to server github and rides a server-wide github grant.

repros.verbatim: grant ["github.read_file"]; register a server named github.read_file exposing any tool -> the whole server is authorized.
repros.source: GitHub the-metafactory/cortex, issue comment 5084213029, finding F4
repros.outcome: Reproduced by this corpus's unit-import check: decideMcp("mcp__github.read_file__x", ["github.read_file"]) returns allow:true. parseMcpToolName splits only on '__', so a server literally named "github.read_file" is parsed whole as the server segment, and it string-equals the per-tool grant "github.read_file" meant for a DIFFERENT server's single tool.

repros.verbatim: a server named github__evil (tool mcp__github__evil__x) parses to server github and rides a server-wide github grant.
repros.source: GitHub the-metafactory/cortex, issue comment 5084213029, finding F4
repros.outcome: Reproduced by this corpus's unit-import check: decideMcp("mcp__github__evil__x", ["github"]) returns allow:true, parsing server="github", tool="evil__x" and matching the server-wide grant.

expected: The server/tool boundary in the grant grammar must be unambiguous regardless of what a connected MCP server happens to be named — either by forbidding '.' and '__' in configured/recognized MCP server names, or by canonicalizing the grant grammar (e.g. an explicit delimiter reserved and validated at both grant-authoring and server-registration time) so a crafted server name cannot collide with a differently-scoped grant.

verification.note: Unit-imports decideMcp and parseMcpToolName from mcp-guard.hook.ts and calls decideMcp directly with both of the finding's own repro shapes. Asserts BOTH currently return allow:true — i.e. this check expects the vulnerability to reproduce, matching status:open. A future fix should flip these to allow:false, which is the signal to update this case's status.
